Abnormally dry conditions (D0) decreased to 12%, moderate drought (D1) remained near 8%, severe drought (D2) increased to 13.5%, extreme drought (D3) increased to near 18%, and exceptional drought (D4) decreased to near 35%.
02/20/2023: Compared to last week, feeder steers overall sold 2.00 to 5.00 higher. Feeder heifers under 500 lbs sold 3.00 to 4.00 lower; over 500 lbs sold 1.00 to 4.00 higher. Slaughter cows and bulls sold 8.00 to 10.00 higher. Demand overall was good. Compared to last week, fed slaughter steers and heifers in the feedyards sold 1.00 to 2.00 higher at 162.00. In the hay market, demand remained good, prices remained steady, trade activity was slow to moderate. Producers state that the hay business has slowed down and are mostly moving previously purchased hay. Finding hay to purchase remains difficult and many are holding on to the hay they have till we get a little closer to spring.
02/13/2023: Compared to last week, feeder steers and heifers under 700 lbs sold on a light test with a lower undertone noted; over 700 lbs sold uneven, 2.00 lower to 2.00 higher. Slaughter cows overall sold 1.00 to 2.00 higher. Slaughter bulls sold steady. Demand overall was moderate to good. Compared to last week, fed slaughter steers and heifers in the feedyards sold 2.00 higher from 160.00 to 161.00. In the hay market, demand remained good, prices remained mostly steady with a slight undertone of softness to round bales of alfalfa. Trade activity was slow to moderate. Finding hay to purchase remains difficult and anyone who raises hay and cattle is definitely hanging on to the hay.
02/06/2023: Compared to last week, feeder steers under 700 lbs sold on a light test with a higher undertone; over 700 lbs sold 2.00 to 4.00 higher. Feeder heifers under 600 lbs sold on a light test with a higher undertone; over 600 lbs steady to 1.00 higher. Slaughter cows overall sold steady to 1.00 lower. Slaughter bulls sold steady to 2.00 lower. Demand overall was good. Compared to last week, fed slaughter steers and heifers in the feedyards sold 2.00 to 3.00 higher from 158.00 to 159.00. In the hay market, demand remained good, prices remained steady, and trade activity was slow to moderate. Folks are still looking to purchase hay but there just isn't much out there to purchase.
01/30/2023: Compared to last week, feeder steers under 600 lbs sold 5.00 to 8.00 higher; 600 to 700 lbs steady to 1.00 lower; over 700 lbs 3.00 to 5.00 higher. Feeder heifers overall sold 5.00 to 8.00 higher. Slaughter cows sold uneven; breaker and boner steady to 3.00 higher, lean 10.00 to 11.00 higher. Slaughter bulls sold 8.00 to 11.00 higher. Demand overall was good. Compared to last week, fed slaughter steers and heifers in the feedyards sold 1.00 higher at 156.00. In the hay market, demand remained good, prices remained steady, and trade activity was moderate. The market remains quiet with previously purchased hay being delivered.
01/23/2023: Compared to last week, feeder steers under 700 lbs sold 6.00 to 8.00 higher; over 700 lbs sold steady to 1.00 higher. Feeder heifers overall sold steady to 5.00 higher. Slaughter cows sold uneven; breaker 8.00 to 10.00 higher, boner and lean 1.00 to 4.00 higher. Slaughter bulls sold steady. Demand overall was good. Fed slaughter steers and heifers in the feedyards sold steady at 155.00. In the hay market, demand remained good, prices remained steady, and trade activity was moderate. Seems as though the hay market is currently in kind of a holding pattern, after the frenzy between August to December. There still is some alfalfa out there to buy but it is pretty hit or miss, and several folks are looking to purchase grass hay, to help get them through. A winter storm system moved across the state last week bringing much needed rain and snow to many.
01/16/2023: Compared to last week, feeder steers overall sold 3.00 to 4.00 lower. Feeder heifers overall sold 3.00 to 6.00 lower. Slaughter cows sold steady to 2.00 higher. Slaughter bulls sold 1.00 to 2.00 lower. Demand overall was moderate. Compared to last week, fed slaughter steers and heifers in the feedyards sold 2.00 lower at 155.00. In the hay market, demand remained strong, prices remained mostly steady, and actual trades were up for the south-central region. Conversations last week revolved around questions regarding a softening market. Although there were discussions, actual prices reported remained firm. Many agree that if precipitation is not received within the next 30 days, they will be up against "the trouble line" which may result in the selling off of cattle. Conversely, southeastern Kansas farmers would like to be in the fields but have found them too soft to begin their work, despite the drought situation.
01/09/2023: Compared to last week, feeder steers overall sold 1.00 to 5.00 lower. Feeder heifers overall sold steady to 2.00 lower, with the exception of 600 to 700 lbs selling 1.00 higher. Slaughter cows sold uneven; breakers and boners 1.00 to 2.00 lower, leans 4.00 to 5.00 lower. Slaughter bulls sold 3.00 to 4.00 lower. Demand overall was good. Compared to last week, fed slaughter steers and heifers in the feedyards sold steady at 157.00. In the hay market, demand remained strong, prices remained mostly steady, but actual trades were down in most regions last week.
01/02/2023: No Feeder cattle or Slaughter Cattle auctions were reported in Kansas last week, so no trend is available. Compared to last week, fed slaughter steers and heifers in the feedyards sold 1.00 higher at 157.00. In the hay market, demand remained strong and prices strengthened, in all regions, ahead of the Christmas holiday and the anticipated winter storm. Producers and brokers continue to report that there is a lot of hay moving and that was reflected in the amount of total hay bought or sold last week. A little rain was received across the state but once again, for those in Southwest Kansas, conditions remain dire with little moisture received.
